Subject: Post-call: SLOs, throughput targets & topology options for Citrine Labs

Hi Evan / Sanjay — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical workshop next Thursday. I focused the notes on the three areas we agreed matter most for the evaluation: latency SLOs, peak throughput, and deployment/topology constraints.

Key pain points you described:
- Inference tail latency causes poor UX on autocomplete flows (users abandon after ~300–400ms).
- Monthly token budget is a hard constraint — need to keep unit cost predictable.
- Data residency: production traffic must remain inside their us-east VPC; logs and trace exports can be pushed to a locked S3 bucket under Citrine's account.

Goals we agreed on:
- Target p95 generation latency <= 300 ms for single-turn generation at median prompt length (~75 tokens).
- Support sustained peak of ~180 concurrent sessions (estimates from your traffic model) with headroom for 30% burst.
- Preserve model-quality comparable to the open Llama-family 33B baseline while reducing cost via quantization/kv-cache.

Model & workload assumptions (for sizing):
- Primary model family: open-weights Llama-2 style 33B (you'll run small internal evals this week).
- Typical prompt + response token profile: 75 tokens prompt / 150 tokens generated.
- Percent of requests that require streaming: ~20% (chat/assistant flows).

Proposed topology options (high level):
1) Redwood Private (VPC Deploy, production): dedicated pool of 4x A100-like nodes with dynamic batching + prefix KV cache; autoscale triggers for burst to additional dedicated capacity.
2) Hybrid (staging hosted, prod Private): onboarding in hosted for integration then private for production to satisfy data residency.
3) On-prem appliance (only if your security team requires air-gapped): will require additional lead time for network/hardening review.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Citrine team: share the small evaluation prompt set and a week of anonymized traffic samples (p95 request size distribution). We discussed a stub S3 upload. (Evan)
- Redwood: deliver a short SLO sizing matrix + topology diagram by EOD tomorrow and a pre-read before the workshop. (Monica / Karthik) — attaching a preliminary SLO matrix and topology sketch to start the conversation.
- Set a 45-min technical workshop: proposed Thu 30 Jun at 15:00 ET. Confirm if that works.

Attachments: citrine_slo_matrix.xlsx, network_topology_v1.png, redwood_configuration_notes.md

Thanks — Vivek

Thanks Vivek — that summary is exactly what we need. A few clarifications from our side to make the SLO sizing useful: 

1) p95 target — we were aiming for p95 <= 275 ms for the primary assistant flow. If meeting 275 is a hard constraint for the UX team, please flag the minimal topology you think will hit that target.
2) Concurrency: 180 sustained is correct; our internal spikes can hit ~250 qps for short windows (2–4 minutes). We'll need a recommended autoscale policy that accounts for warm KV cache vs cold-start penalty.
3) Data residency: production inference nodes must be in our us-east-1 VPC. Logs/traces can be exported to our S3 with encryption keys we control (we'll supply KMS ARNs).

Also: security wants to know if Redwood can provide a SOC2 report and a short list of required firewall ports for an inbound model-serving mesh. If you can include that in the pre-read, great.

We confirm Thu 30 Jun 15:00 ET for the workshop. I'll upload the sample traffic (anonymized) to the folder you shared by tomorrow noon.

Cheers,
Evan

Evan — thanks for the signal. Short technical notes from our side to set expectations before the workshop: 

- Hitting p95 <= 275 ms at ~150 tokens gen for an open 33B family model typically requires: dedicated low-latency NVLink-connected GPU instances (we commonly recommend 4x A100-sim equivalent with optimized kernels) OR model quantization to int4 with optimized kernels + KV cache. If you want strict 275 ms with minimal nodes, quantized model + aggressive batching is the practical approach, but we should validate quality tradeoffs on your prompt set.
- Cold-start penalty: if a model replica is cold (no KV cache), we see initial 2–3x latency on first few tokens — that's why parallelism/warm pools and lightweight prefix caching are important.
- Autoscale policy suggestion: maintain a warm baseline to cover 75% sustained concurrency; scale additional replicas when queue depth exceeds 50ms tail across 3 measurement windows. We'll draft a concrete policy in the pre-read.

I'll attach a quick network-port checklist and SOC2 pointer. Also note that Private VPC deploys require a small connector (outbound-only control plane) and inbound-only port rules for health checks if you want push metrics; we'll include the exact port list.

I'll follow up with a short technical pre-read (10–12 slides) and a suggested sizing matrix tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Monica
